rounds.fact: USA Today's website carried over the newspaper's signature colorful infographics and short-story format, designed for readers scanning quickly rather than reading in depth.
Hotmail was one of the first free webmail services, launched in 1996, and grew largely because every outgoing email carried a tagline advertising the service itself.
Charles Schwab was one of the first traditional brokerages to fully embrace online trading, helping legitimize the idea for investors who didn't trust newer online-only upstarts.
PayPal originally grew by paying users real money just to sign up and refer friends, an aggressive growth tactic that helped it become the dominant way to pay on eBay.
Engadget launched in 2004 and quickly became one of the most-read gadget blogs, known for live-blogging tech keynotes years before that became a standard practice across tech media.
